reason: The disk and hot inner orbits suggest a direct route toward the inner rocky mixture.
expectation: This should distinguish or produce material in the hot inner disk.

effect: The young Sun, rather than hot inner orbits directly, establishes the disk's temperature gradient; I can now work with the hot inner region.
reaction: The compatibility feedback made the failed guess useful.
reason: Rock-forming dust in the heated inner disk looks like a plausible route to the rocky mixture.

choice.combine: A disk with a hot inner region

expectation: The dust should form or contribute to an inner-disk rocky mixture.

effect: The hot inner orbits evaporated the inherited grains, so the rocky mixture must develop from reprocessed material.
reaction: I was surprised that the grains vaporized rather than immediately forming the mixture.
reason: The vapor could have several possible next steps, so checking its partners will help avoid another blind guess.
expectation: The inspection should reveal how the vapor can be processed further.

alternatives.reason: Escaping radiation might cool the vapor enough for solids to form.

effect: Cooling the vapor produced refractory mineral grains, which can contribute to the inner disk's rocky mixture.
reaction: It is satisfying to see solids condense again after the earlier grains evaporated.
reason: Iron-bearing metal grains are a plausible component to combine with the newly condensed minerals for the rocky mixture.
expectation: The mineral and metal grains should contribute to an inner-disk rocky mixture.

effect: The refractory grains joined rock-forming dust to make a rocky aggregate; iron-bearing grains were not the indicated partner.
reaction: The mixture of grains with different histories is an interesting detail.
reason: The aggregate may still need further processing for the inner-disk goal, so checking its available partners should clarify the next step.
expectation: The inspection should reveal how the aggregate can be used next.

effect: Brief intense heating melted the aggregate into droplets; they likely need to cool before contributing to the rocky mixture.
reaction: Leaving the heating mechanism open is a useful scientific qualification.
reason: Escaping radiation previously cooled vapor into grains, so it is a plausible way to solidify the droplets.
expectation: The droplets should cool and solidify into rocky grains.

effect: The droplets cooled into chondrules, which may now join other grains in the inner-disk mixture.
reaction: Their textures preserving evidence of rapid heating and cooling are an interesting detail.
reason: Iron-bearing metal grains remain available and are a plausible partner for the cooled rocky chondrules.
expectation: The chondrules and metal grains should contribute to the inner-disk rocky mixture.

effect: The chondrules and metal formed the rocky mixture, completing the inner-disk goal; ice storage remains.
reaction: It is useful to distinguish a mixture of ingredients from a formed planet.
reason: Ice-mantled dust and cold outer orbits are the visible ingredients for storing ice beyond the snow line.
expectation: The cold outer region should preserve the ice-bearing dust.

effect: The ice-mantled dust instead sublimated in hot inner orbits, producing water vapor; the outer ice-storage route remains unclear.
reaction: The automatic warm-orbit result was unexpected when I tried the cold orbits.
reason: The water vapor may have a route back to colder regions, so checking its partners is more useful than another guess.
expectation: The inspection should reveal whether the vapor can move or cool into an ice-bearing region.

effect: Water vapor moved into cold outer orbits and recondensed; the resulting ice may need another step to complete storage.
reaction: The water's movement and recondensation clarified how the disk reprocesses inherited ice.
reason: The ice has not yet completed the goal, so checking its available partners should reveal how to store it.
expectation: The inspection should reveal the next available use for the outer-disk ice.

effect: The recondensed ice joined inherited ice-mantled dust, completing the outer-disk store and the chapter.
reaction: Seeing inherited and reprocessed ice together brought the water’s route to a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the rocky material from vapor through condensed grains and heated droplets to chondrules was worthwhile: it showed how material can be reprocessed and retain evidence of its history.

leastWorthwhile.text: The repeated compatibility checks became somewhat mechanical, especially when they automatically performed the only available operation.

surprise.text: I expected ice-mantled dust to work directly with cold outer orbits, but the feedback sent it through sublimation first; the vapor then recondensed farther out.

arbitrary.text: The required warm-orbit detour felt arbitrary when I was trying to store existing ice in the cold outer disk, even though the result explained a plausible reprocessing route.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the rocky mixture and ice-bearing dust become larger bodies, particularly if the story continues explaining the underlying processes.
